solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S049-01.notes: Report detailed costs/benefits but declined to take a position = noncommittal. A partisan contradicts declining to take a side. B redundant has no support (no repetition mentioned). D inflammatory contradicts the neutral, measured report.

S049-02.notes: Text sets up a puzzle (why Roman concrete lasts) and gives the researchers' explanation. B: no recommendation is made. C: no later empires mentioned. D: mining methods not discussed; ash is mentioned only as an ingredient.

S049-03.notes: Hypothesis is social learning (learning by observing other crows). Crows hatched after the captures that were never captured themselves but still scold the mask can only have learned it from others. A: stresses direct experience and does not show learning from others. B: about scolding at a distance, not how the crows learned. C: about the neutral mask, irrelevant to the learning route.

S049-04.notes: The caution follows from the sampling limits: observers stayed on trails and could hear only about 50 m, so the survey cannot show how species numbers change away from trails. A and D draw the very causal/preference conclusion the caution warns against. C: the dawn timing is not the limitation cited, and 'only time' is unsupported.

S049-05.notes: Text 2 raises a self-selection/generalizability objection: the firms may be atypical. A contradicts his skepticism. B: he does not dispute that the gains happened. D: worker preferences are not discussed.

flags.note: A is the only option that gives counts, and it restates both parts of the claim, so it is easy to spot without doing the arithmetic. Still, it is a fair quantitative-evidence item.

S049-06.notes: 0.20*800=160 urban vs 0.30*200=60 rural, so more urban residents even though their percentage is lower. B gives only the percentages, which favor rural. C gives sample sizes but no counts of 'yes' answers. D does not compare the groups.

S049-07.notes: With either/or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'coauthors' (plural), so the answer is 'are'. Present tense fits 'next month'. A, C and D are all singular verbs; C and D also clash in tense with the future event.

S049-08.notes: The introductory participial phrase must modify the person who spent the decade, so 'the historian' must be the subject: 'the historian concluded that...'. A and C make the conclusion the subject (dangling modifier). B makes 'it' the subject in a passive construction, which also dangles.

S049-09.notes: The second sentence gives a concrete detail of 'far heavier traffic' (40 tons, twice the old limit), so 'Specifically' fits. A: no contrast. B: nothing is replaced or rejected. D: the sentence elaborates on the first rather than presenting a parallel similar point.

flags.note: The phrase 'carry more water than any other rivers' is loose. The notes support that the two rivers rank first and second in discharge, and the sentence can be read as saying that, but tighter wording such as 'carry the two largest volumes of water of any rivers' would be clearer. 'vast' slightly upgrades the notes' 'large'. Neither problem changes the key.

S049-10.notes: Only D states something the two rivers share (both drain rainforests, both are top discharge rivers). A and C contrast the two rivers. B describes the Congo alone, and 'unusually deep' goes beyond the notes.
